Yes — this fits the site well, actually. The site is 100% static (no build, no framework, no server state beyond one Vercel function for NIP-05), and NDK's whole model is "relays are the backend," so there's no server to build — comments and highlights just become nostr events fetched/published client-side.

How it'd map:
- **Comments**: NIP-22 (`kind:1111`) anchored via NIP-73 external-content tags (`I`/`K` = the essay's canonical URL, since the essay pages aren't nostr events themselves) — read by filtering `#I` on that URL, threaded by `e`/`E` for replies.
- **Highlights**: NIP-84 (`kind:9802`), content = selected text, `r` tag = canonical URL, `context` tag = surrounding paragraph. Select text → "Highlight" button → publish.
- **Writing**: NIP-07 browser-extension signing (Alby, nos2x) via `NDKNip07Signer` — no login system needed, reading needs no signer at all.

Main tradeoff: since there's zero build pipeline today, I'd either load NDK straight from a CDN (jsDelivr/esm.sh, simplest, but resolves deps at runtime on every visit) or prebuild a small bundle locally once (esbuild) and commit the output `.js` as a static asset (faster, pinned, but means running a build step by hand whenever the widget code changes — not on every deploy, just when I edit it).

**Fixed and verified.** The bug you hit — clicking "Highlight" doing nothing, not even prompting a signature — was a real DOM race: the global `mouseup` listener that opens the toolbar wasn't ignoring mouseup events that landed on the toolbar itself, so clicking it destroyed-and-recreated the button mid-click, which silently suppresses the browser's `click` event on the now-detached original element. Added a guard (`f7z.io/src/highlights.js`) so the listener ignores mouseup events originating inside `.n-hl-toolbar`, rebuilt `js/highlights.js`, and re-ran the full flow in a real browser with a fake NIP-07 provider: sign-in → select text → click Highlight → `<mark class="n-highlight">` appears wrapping the selection → hover tooltip shows the highlighter's name/npub and timestamp. All confirmed working.

Summary of what's shipped on the `attention`/`memory`/`structure`/`citizens`/`zero` essay pages:
- **Build**: `npm run build` (esbuild) bundles `src/highlights.js` + NDK into the committed static `js/highlights.js` (~355KB minified, loaded via `<script defer>`, no runtime CDN dependency).
- **Sign-in**: floating bottom-right pill, only rendered if a NIP-07 extension is detected; shows avatar/name once signed in, click to sign out; silently re-signs-in on return visits via a localStorage flag.
- **Highlights**: signed-in users select text → "Highlight" pill → publishes a NIP-84 (`kind:9802`) event tagged to the essay's canonical URL, wrapped locally right away (optimistic, doesn't wait on relay confirmation).
- **Reading**: on load, subscribes for existing highlights on that URL from four public relays and marks up matching text in place, with a hover tooltip showing who highlighted it and when.

Verified working end-to-end with real relay data. Summary of what's shipped on `/feed/`:

- Every `.post` card is now clickable (except the "view on nostr" link, which still navigates normally) and opens a slide-in panel — reusing the same `.detail-panel`/`.detail-backdrop` chrome already used on `/nownownow/`.
- The panel shows the clicked post cloned as the OP, then subscribes live via NDK for `kind:1` events tagging that note's id across four public relays, rendering each as a `.post`-styled reply card (avatar, name/nip05, relative timestamp, content, its own "view on nostr" link) — a flat, Twitter-style conversation view.
- Confirmed with a real browser test: real replies loaded from actual relays, empty/loading states behave correctly, panel state doesn't leak between posts, and the nostr-link click doesn't get swallowed by the new handler.
- Built via `src/feed-thread.js` → `js/feed-thread.js` (same local-esbuild-bundle pattern as the highlights feature), ~352KB minified, loaded with `defer`.

One known simplification worth flagging: it fetches *all* kind:1 events tagging the post via `#e`, without NIP-10 marker filtering — so a rare quote-post that merely mentions the note (rather than replying to it) could show up alongside true replies.
